memo:
EdgeHound Performance Review — 14 June 2026

The bot has drawn down 14.3% from inception ($10K → $8,574 equity), with realized losses of -$1,576 across 21 closed trades. The core problem is unambiguous: MOMENTUM is the primary bleeding engine, producing 5W/13L (-$1,249 realized) on 18 trades — a 28% win rate against an implied breakeven near 46% at these stake/stop configurations. The Brier score of 0.298 confirms systematically poor probability calibration; the model is confidently wrong.

Several structural problems stand out. First, MOMENTUM took repeated concentrated positions on Iran geopolitical markets ($150–$350 each, multiple entries on the same event), all stopped out — a correlated cluster that looks like one bad thesis repeated six times with no circuit-breaker. Second, large individual stakes ($800) were deployed on single sports events (Trungelliti, Udvardy, Bouzkova) with only an 18% profit target against a 20% stop, giving a roughly 0.9:1 reward/risk ratio — structurally negative EV even at 50% win rates. Third, SMART_CONSENSUS placed a $1,000 stake on an esports match that hit -30% stop within the same hour of entry — position sizing was wildly inconsistent with a $500 maxEventExposure rail, suggesting a prior config permitted it.

The prior analyst session already disabled MOMENTUM and SMART_CONSENSUS and cut kellyMult to 0.10. These are the correct moves. I will maintain that posture, tighten maxEventExposure to $500 to prevent recurrence of outsized single-event bets, and keep pMin at 0.62. SHORT_FAVORITE's small positive PnL (+$58, 1W/1L) is encouraging but sample size is trivial. VOLUME_SPIKE and ELITE_FOLLOW remain enabled but inactive — no changes warranted.
